messages:
marta: ap-northeast canaries started failing TRT engine builds after the driver rollout this morning. nvrtc/ptx mismatch in logs. @sam @ops-bot :eyes:
sam: looking. which driver version was pushed?
deploy-bot: driver-rollout: nodes in ap-northeast-1 pool updated to NVIDIA driver 541.22 at 08:13 UTC
marta: here's a pod log snippet: ```TRT: Engine creation failed: NVRTC error - JIT_SOURCE_PROCESSING failed: ptx version mismatch: compiled for ptx 10.2, driver supports 9.0```
sam: hmm — 541 should support newer PTX. maybe our container bundles an older nvrtc that doesn't match system libnvrtc. which image is this?
devon: image is `a100-prod:trt8.2.0-2024-11` (we pinned it). suspect libcuda/libnvrtc ABI mismatch after kernel/driver change.
lina: also seeing some multi-GPU jobs in eu-west stuck on all-reduce around the same time window, but drivers there are still 540.x — could be unrelated networking jitter.
kai: possible explanation: TRT's nvrtc picks either bundled or host nvrtc; driver change altered JIT behavior. quick probe: `ldd /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvinfer.so | grep nvrtc`
sam: running a probe on canary-3: `ssh canary-3 && docker run --rm --entrypoint bash a100-prod:trt8.2 -c 'python -c "import ctypes, os; print(os.environ.get(\"LD_LIBRARY_PATH\"))"'`
ops-bot: canary snapshot uploaded: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/canary/1854321000/snapshot.tar.gz
marta: workaround options: (1) force container to use host nvrtc via bind-mount, (2) roll the driver back in ap-northeast canaries, or (3) rebuild TRT image against the shipped nvrtc.
devon: I'll open a rollback PR for the ap-northeast nodepool (flip driverVersion -> 540.36) and apply to canaries first.
sam: also opening TRT support ticket — will attach `nvidia-smi -q`, `/var/log/nvrtc_*` and the failing pod logs.
lina: on the NCCL hang side I collected socket traces; seeing increased TCP retransmits between pods during the 08:00-08:20 window. tagging @net-team.
jen: net-team update: we rolled an accelerated path on one rack in ap-northeast for perf tests; we didn't change MTU, but we did toggle SR-IOV on a rack — could explain transient egress behavior.
marta: plan: devon -> rollback drivers in ap-northeast canaries and validate TRT builds; sam -> open TRT ticket with logs; lina -> continue NCCL trace work; ops-bot -> pause global driver rollout. :thumbsup:
sam: quick test: I'll try mounting host `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` into the container to force host nvrtc and see if engine builds succeed.
devon: rollback PR created: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/driver-rolls/pull/412, applying to canary-3 now
ops-bot: driver-rollout: pausing global rollout at stage 3 per @marta
marta: update: after rollback on canary-3, TRT engine build now passes. still watching some long-tail NCCL jobs but canary looks good. marking incident in-progress and will keep channel updated.
